mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of more than 0.5% in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month + 0.5% AND HOUST > previous month + 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months signals an extended period of monetary accommodation, which lowers borrowing costs and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for at least six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly rise of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall of more than 0.5% in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.4pp AND PAYEMS < previous month - 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase of more than 0.7% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 0.7% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
